title: UniCache: Unifying Prefix Cache Eviction for Heterogeneous LLM Serving Workloads
one_line: A task-aware multi-queue prefix-KV-cache eviction policy for vLLM that combines session-reuse (log-normal inter-turn horizon) and structural-reuse (prompt-offset) signals with a global hit-efficiency weighting, plus a CPU trace-driven prefix-cache simulator built on vLLM's control plane.

repo.evidence: Paper §6 (p. 15) states 'The code is available at https://github.com/xsyslab/UniCache'; xsyslab is last author Jiarong Xing's lab org (Rice). The repo is a vLLM v0.8.5 fork containing the actual policy (vllm/core/evictor.py:1254 SimpleHYBRIDEvictor implementing Alg. 1, :1702 implementing Alg. 2) and the §3 simulator (vllm/simulator/).
repo.badge_evidence: none found - no AE appendix or badge in the camera-ready PDF, none on the SIGMETRICS'26 abstract page (https://doi.org/10.1145/3801489.3806861)

H1_open_repo.evidence: Official repo linked from the paper (§6, p. 15). Contains the full system, not a stub: vllm/core/evictor.py:1254 (SimpleHYBRIDEvictor, two-stage eviction at :1429, queue assignment at :1302, local priority at :1214), :1702 (hit-efficiency alpha update), all 7 baselines (LRU:265, LFU:529, FIFO:605, WA:375, LeCaR:962, ARC:694, OPT:100) and the simulator (vllm/simulator/simulator.py, output_simulator.py).

H2_no_root.evidence: Headline path is 'python run_simulation.py' on CPU. vllm/engine/llm_engine.py:288-292 skips model_executor construction and :496-497 skips KV-cache allocation in simulation mode; run_simulation.py:188 uses load_format='dummy'; vllm/_custom_ops.py:17-21 tolerates a missing compiled vllm._C. The sudo / kernel-module / RDMA / multi-GPU grep hits in repo_facts.json are all inherited upstream vLLM CI and docs (.github/workflows/scripts/cuda-install.sh, .buildkite/*, docs/source/getting_started/installation/ai_accelerator/neuron.inc.md) and are not on the artifact's run path. docker/Dockerfile is upstream vLLM's and is replaced by the conda recipe in README.md:35-78. No perf counters, eBPF, KVM or /proc/sys writes.

H3_hardware_fit.evidence: Paper §6.1: 'We conducted latency experiments (Section 6.4) on real GPUs, while the remaining results were obtained from our simulator' - Fig. 10, Fig. 11 and Fig. 12 are CPU-only and need no GPU (A100/H200 labels only set the block budget). 16 cores / 125 GB RAM suffice (§3.3 reports ~150 s per simulated trace). The single-GPU QTTFT result (Table 5, one A100, Llama-3.1-3B) scales down to the 24 GB A5000 because run_gpu.py:255 also uses load_format='dummy' and the block budget is a CLI knob (assertion at vllm/engine/llm_engine.py:452 only requires real blocks >= requested). tensor_parallel_size defaults to 1 (run_simulation.py:120); §6.6 states the policy is TP-agnostic. No multi-node requirement.

H4_obtainable_deps_data.evidence: Deps are pip/conda only (requirements/common.txt, requirements/cpu.txt, README.md:63-75; CPU torch 2.6.0, transformers 4.53.2). Datasets are public: ShareGPT via HF wget (TaskData/SharedGPT-multi-turn/readme.md:4), AgentBank via load_dataset('Solaris99/AgentBank') (TaskData/AgentBankData/prepare_agentbank_data.py:28), CodeParrot via datasets (TaskData/Codeparrot/prepare_data.py:8), MASH-QA via the authors' Google Drive (TaskData/mashqa_data/readme.md:2), ToolBench via the public Preble OneDrive share (TaskData/ToolBench/readme.md:1). The proprietary Qwen-Bailian production trace is not needed - it was only used to fit (mu, sigma), and the constants are hard-coded at vllm/core/evictor.py:1177-1183 and duplicated in the yaml configs. models/download.sh pulls UNGATED unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and unsloth/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct mirrors with --exclude '*.safetensors' - only config + tokenizer are required since weights are dummy.

reproduce.target: Fig. 10(a), p. 18 - Trace #1 (multi-turn-dominant), Llama-3.2-1B: prefix-cache hit ratio vs KV-cache budget for LRU/LFU/FIFO/LeCaR/ARC/WA/OPT-Offline/UniCache. Claim: UniCache is the best online policy at every budget (92.32% vs LRU 91.64%, FIFO 91.19%, LFU 79.42% at 0.7A).
reproduce.scale_down: CPU simulator only, no GPU and no model weights (load_format='dummy'). Use TaskData/Hybrid/test1/tasks_config.yaml with max_record cut 1800 -> 600 for the four single-turn tasks and 500 -> 200 for ShareGPT/alfred, with --simulator-num-gpu-blocks scaled down proportionally so the working-set/cache ratio (and hence the cache-pressure regime) is preserved; sweep 3 budgets (50000/70000/100000 blocks at --block-size 8) x 8 policies = 24 runs instead of the paper's 9-panel grid. Report policy ordering and the UniCache-LRU gap rather than absolute hit ratios, since the paper's 0.5A/0.7A/0.9A axis has no documented mapping to block counts. Re-run at full trace size once the pipeline works.
reproduce.effort: ~5 person-days + ~30 CPU-core-hours (0 GPU-hours); add ~2 person-days + ~8 GPU-hours if the optional Table 5 QTTFT check on the A5000 is attempted
reproduce.rationale: The exact result runs on CPU with no root, no gated data and no compilation (llm_engine.py:288-292 skips the executor, _custom_ops.py:17-21 tolerates the missing extension), and a 20-session smoke test ships in-repo (demo/run.sh + demo/ShareGPT_cleaned_valid_session_data_head20.jsonl) - that argues for H. Capped at M by real porting work: (i) no aggregation/plotting script exists for Fig. 10 (only per-run summary.json and a per-run histogram in vllm/simulator/utils.py); (ii) TaskData/Hybrid/test{2..9}/run.sh and test1/run_opt.sh pass --tag and --enable-hybrid-opt, which run_simulation.py's argparse (lines 16-139) does not define, so they abort as shipped; (iii) the paper's budget axis must be re-derived from per-token KV footprint; (iv) five external datasets (HF, Google Drive, a personal OneDrive) must be fetched and tokenized first; (v) model paths in the sweep scripts are absolute to the authors' machine and the conda path in README.md:41 is hard-coded; (vi) platform auto-detection (vllm/platforms/__init__.py:50-75) will pick the CUDA platform on our GPU host even for a CPU run, and the demo's VLLM_PLATFORM=cpu is not a variable this vLLM version reads.

addons.name: Kill the task-label oracle
addons.hypothesis: We hypothesize that replacing UniCache's oracle task labels with an online, content-derived classifier (turn-index observation for session reuse plus radix-prefix template signatures for structural reuse) retains most of UniCache's hit-ratio gain over LRU on Traces #1-#3, and that the gain degrades gracefully rather than catastrophically as label error rises.
addons.mechanism: Today the task type is a hard-coded session-id string comparison ('alfred_' -> MULTI_TURN_AGENTIC, 'apps_'/'mind2web_' -> SINGLE_TURN_RANDOM i.e. straight into the evict-first queue) and the same mapping drives per-queue hit accounting. Replace it with a TaskClassifier that sees only admission-time signals: (a) a request whose longest prefix match lands inside a live session chain is multi-turn, and the observed inter-arrival gap separates chat from agentic; (b) single-turn requests are bucketed by the hash of their first k blocks (template signature), and buckets whose measured reuse rate stays below a threshold are demoted to the evict-first queue - exactly what SINGLE_TURN_RANDOM does by fiat today. Then sweep injected label noise p = 0..0.5 to produce a sensitivity curve.
addons.motivating_evidence: §6.6 ('Task type classification') asserts categories 'can often be inferred from lightweight signals ... such as request metadata' but no experiment uses an inferred label; the artifact hard-codes ground truth at prefix_caching_block.py:1019-1034. Implication 3 and the evict-first queue (which contains ALL untemplated single-turn prefill blocks, §5.2) depend entirely on that label, and Table 1 (p. 2) already shows a mis-targeted policy can be worse than LRU for a whole task class.
addons.feasibility_rationale: Entirely inside the simulator, ~500-1000 LOC, no new harness - the existing tasks_config.yaml traces and summary.json hit-ratio output are exactly the measurement needed, and label noise is a one-line perturbation. CPU only, fits 2-4 students in 10 weeks with room to spare.
addons.research_value_rationale: This is the load-bearing assumption of the whole design and the first thing a SIGMETRICS reviewer would poke at. Both outcomes teach: 'UniCache survives realistic labelling' makes it deployable; 'it does not' reframes the paper's 17.32% as an oracle upper bound.

scoop_check.details: Searched 'UniCache prefix cache eviction heterogeneous LLM serving follow-up', 'KV cache prefix cache admission control never-reused blocks 2026', 'per-tenant fairness prefix KV cache eviction 2026'. Closest: SAECache, arXiv 2605.18825 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18825), a concurrent May-2026 preprint with a near-identical multi-queue design that infers multi-turn session type with a ~1M-param MLP over the model's last-layer hidden state - but it needs model internals (unavailable in the CPU simulator), releases no code, and never cites or compares against UniCache. PEEK, arXiv 2607.02525 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.02525), builds radix-tree prefix clusters for admission/eviction, overlapping the template-signature half but not the label-sensitivity study.

addons.name: Latency-aware value instead of hit-token value
addons.hypothesis: We hypothesize that replacing UniCache's hit-token-per-capacity efficiency with a recompute-cost-per-capacity value - cost estimated by the paper's own power-law prefill model, and charged for the suffix blocks an eviction strands - reduces mean and p90 QTTFT on single-turn-dominant and long-prompt-heavy traffic (Trace #3 / MASH-QA-heavy mixes) at equal or slightly lower hit ratio.
addons.mechanism: Two local changes. (1) In update_alpha_balance, replace H_q (a raw count of hit tokens) with the sum of modelled prefill time for those hits, using the same a*BS^b*L^c expression the simulator already evaluates: a 2000-token document hit is worth super-linearly more wall-clock than 2000 tokens spread over 40 chat turns, yet the current metric prices them identically. (2) In calculate_priority, charge an eviction for its dependent suffix: strict prefix matching means evicting an early block makes every cached descendant unreachable, so a block's value should include its still-resident descendant count, which the existing prefix trie in the block manager can supply cheaply.
addons.motivating_evidence: The paper optimizes hit ratio and reports QTTFT only once (Table 5, p. 19: one model, one budget, 0.9A). The two do not track each other - on Trace #3 UniCache is 0.10 s vs ARC 0.12 s (17% gap) while the average hit-ratio gap over ARC is quoted as 3.86%, and OPT-Offline reaches 0.08 s. §5.2's tail-first ordering (Implication 5, Fig. 8a) is justified precisely by suffix invalidation, yet the §5.3 value metric never accounts for it.
addons.feasibility_rationale: ~300-600 LOC across two functions plus a descendant counter; the virtual clock already yields QTTFT in simulation and the hit-ratio harness is unchanged. CPU only.
addons.research_value_rationale: Cost/size-aware caching (GDSF and descendants) is well-trodden, so some win is expected. The non-obvious parts are whether the stranded-suffix term dominates the cost term and whether hit ratio and latency diverge enough to reorder the policy ranking - interesting but incremental.

scoop_check.details: Searched 'cost-aware prefix cache eviction suffix invalidation trie LLM GDSF size-aware KV block' and 'hotness-aware KV cache scheduling prefix caching'. CacheWise (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.16824) and Hotness-Aware KV Cache Scheduling (https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3749168) use recompute-cost-weighted priorities, but neither does so inside a task-partitioned multi-queue policy and neither models the stranded-suffix term.

addons.name: Distribution shift vs hard-coded reuse horizons
addons.hypothesis: We hypothesize that UniCache's advantage over LRU shrinks or inverts when the deployed inter-turn interval distribution differs from the offline-fitted (mu, sigma) baked into the policy, and that an online estimator refitted from observed reuse intervals recovers most of the loss without needing historical traces.
addons.mechanism: TASK_CONFIG hard-codes (4.77, 1.279) for chat and (1.81, 1.092) for agentic while the workload generator samples turn gaps from whatever mu/sigma the yaml specifies (test1 uses 4.15/0.971 for ShareGPT - already a mismatch). Step 1: sweep the generator's (mu, sigma) plus bimodal and heavy-tailed variants with the policy's constants fixed, and plot the hit-ratio gap vs LRU against the mismatch. Step 2: wire the policy to an online estimator - wa_helper.py already collects per-task reuse intervals (collect_hit_interval:69) and refits periodically (_fit_all:36) for the WA baseline; swap its exponential fit for a log-normal MLE and have calculate_priority query it. Step 3: an estimator-free variant that ranks multi-turn blocks by the empirical survival function, needing no parametric assumption.
addons.motivating_evidence: §5.2 states the distribution 'can be fitted using historical traces (e.g., data from prior days or from the same weekday in previous weeks)' - an explicit stationarity assumption the evaluation never stresses, since every §6.1 trace is generated from the same log-normal family the policy assumes. Fig. 6 (p. 10) shows chat and agentic horizons differ ~30x in scale (P80 372 s vs 12 s), so the policy is demonstrably sensitive to getting them right.
addons.feasibility_rationale: Step 1 is a yaml sweep on the existing harness with essentially no new code; step 2 reuses an existing helper class (wa_helper.py) and a single call site in calculate_priority. All CPU.
addons.research_value_rationale: The sensitivity characterization is new, cheap and would be a legitimate 'careful reproduction shows a more nuanced result' outcome, but the online-fitting remedy is the obvious fix and a reviewer would expect it to work; a concurrent preprint already reports that fixed-parameter variants degrade under mismatch.

scoop_check.details: Searched 'UniCache ... follow-up' and 'online log-normal reuse interval estimation prefix cache eviction'. SAECache (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18825) already proposes online MLE of per-task (mu, sigma) plus adaptive position decay and queue weights, and reports that 'fixed-parameter alternatives can degrade by up to 2.7x under workload mismatch' - essentially step 2 and part of step 1. It is an unrefereed preprint with no released code that does not cite or compare against UniCache, so a measured study on the UniCache artifact is still a contribution, but the team should lead with the shift characterization and the non-parametric variant rather than with adaptive fitting.

addons.name: Per-task structural queues and a measured position profile
addons.hypothesis: We hypothesize that splitting UniCache's single structural-reuse queue into per-task queues, and replacing the fixed offset normalizer with each task's measured prompt-length distribution, improves hit ratio on single-turn-dominant traffic (Trace #3) by more than the Stage-2 weighting alone.
addons.mechanism: Implication 3 says different single-turn tasks should be managed independently, but the implementation puts ToolBench, CodeParrot and MASH-QA into one 'single' queue with one alpha_single. Worse, the positional score divides by a global constant max_offset = 2048 (self.max_num_first_offset) rather than 'the maximum offset among all blocks' as §5.2 defines it, so for MASH-QA documents beyond 2048 tokens offset_factor saturates at 0 and the in-queue ordering degenerates. Add one queue per single-turn task (the alpha machinery is already dict-keyed), normalize the offset by a running quantile of that task's prompt length, and optionally replace the linear 1 - offset/max_offset with the empirically measured reuse-vs-depth curve (measurable today via --enable-block-hit-track / block_id_2_count).
addons.motivating_evidence: Fig. 7a (p. 10) shows single-turn reuse ratios spanning 0.21% (untemplated) to 61.13% (document QA) - a ~300x spread the implementation collapses into one queue with one weight - and Table 3 (p. 11) shows the four templates have different structures. The fixed 2048 normalizer is a plain implementation/paper mismatch against the §5.2 definition.
addons.feasibility_rationale: Contained within SimpleHYBRIDEvictor, a few hundred LOC, evaluated with the existing Trace #2/#3 configs and summary.json output on CPU.
addons.research_value_rationale: It directly tests the paper's own Implication 3 and repairs a real artifact/paper discrepancy, which is worth reporting, but 'more queues help when tasks differ' is close to what the paper already argues; the surprising outcome would be that it does not help, i.e. that Stage 2 already absorbs the difference.

scoop_check.details: Searched 'per-task queues single-turn structural prefix reuse eviction' and 'position-aware prefix cache eviction offset decay'. SAECache (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18825) learns a position-decay exponent and per-token-type weights, subsuming the positional half of the idea; no work found that separates the structural queue per single-turn task or that reports the max_offset saturation issue.

addons.name: Demote instead of drop: task-aware GPU-to-CPU tiering
addons.hypothesis: We hypothesize that spilling UniCache's evicted blocks into a CPU-DRAM second tier, with the demotion decision driven by the same per-queue hit efficiency, reduces QTTFT relative to dropping them on multi-turn-dominant traffic, and that the benefit inverts once modelled PCIe transfer time exceeds the recompute time for short prefixes.
addons.mechanism: The evictor currently discards the victim block. Add a CPU tier of --simulator-num-cpu-blocks capacity (the flag already exists) holding evicted blocks; on a prefix match that lands in the CPU tier, advance the virtual clock by a modelled transfer (bytes / measured H2D bandwidth) instead of a full prefill, and run a second-level eviction in that tier. Use alpha_q to decide which queues are worth spilling - chat blocks with a 372 s P80 reuse horizon deserve CPU space, agentic blocks with a 12 s horizon may be cheaper to recompute.
addons.motivating_evidence: §7 notes CachedAttention and Pensieve add hierarchical tiers but says nothing about which policy should govern demotion. The artifact already accounts for an LMCache CPU tier in its summary output (simulator.py:482-486, output_simulator.py:87) but the CPU simulation path never exercises it. Fig. 10 hit ratios saturate at large budgets, so the regime where a second tier pays is exactly the small-budget end where UniCache's margin is largest.
addons.feasibility_rationale: Cross-cutting: touches the allocator, the evictor and the timing model, and the transfer-cost model must be calibrated with a few GPU-hours of real H2D KV-block bandwidth measurement on the A5000. Still fits a 10-week 2-4 student budget, but it is not a localized change.
addons.research_value_rationale: Tiered KV caching is crowded, so the placement mechanism itself is not novel; the contribution is coupling the demotion decision to the task-partitioned hit-efficiency signal and characterizing the recompute-vs-transfer crossover, which is of moderate interest.

scoop_check.details: Searched 'task-aware tiered KV cache demotion GPU to CPU prefix cache eviction policy 2026' and 'predictive multi-tier memory management KV cache'. Predictive Multi-Tier Memory Management for KV Cache (https://arxiv.org/html/2604.26968v2) and llm-d's tiered prefix cache do promotion/demotion by predicted access probability; CachedAttention (ATC'24) and Mooncake (FAST'25) cover the storage side. None couples demotion to a task-partitioned hit-efficiency weight, and none is evaluated against UniCache.

risks: Task labels are an oracle: vllm/core/block/prefix_caching_block.py:1019-1034 keys the queue assignment (and the evict-first decision) on session-id string prefixes such as 'ShareGPT-multi-turn', 'alfred_', 'apps_'. Regenerated data with different ids silently falls through to SINGLE_TURN with no error - the biggest reproduction hazard.

Most shipped sweep scripts abort: TaskData/Hybrid/test{2..9}/run.sh and TaskData/Hybrid/test1/run_opt.sh pass --tag and --enable-hybrid-opt, which run_simulation.py's argparse (lines 16-139) does not define. Only TaskData/Hybrid/test1/run.sh matches the current CLI.

No aggregation or plotting pipeline for Fig. 10 / Fig. 11 / Table 5 - only per-run summary.json and a per-run histogram in vllm/simulator/utils.py - and the paper's 0.5A/0.7A/0.9A budget axis has no documented mapping to --simulator-num-gpu-blocks, so absolute hit ratios must be re-derived.

Platform detection: vllm/platforms/__init__.py:50-75 selects the CUDA platform whenever nvml sees a GPU and the installed vllm version string lacks 'cpu', which is our situation; demo/run.sh:3 relies on VLLM_PLATFORM=cpu, a variable this vLLM version does not read (vllm/envs.py:146). Whether the CPU simulator starts cleanly on a GPU host is unverified - this was a desk review, nothing was executed.

vllm/simulator/output_simulator.py:146 appends to tracked_hit_stats once per request forever and vllm/core/evictor.py:1723 sums the whole list every 10 requests; the 'recent time window' of Alg. 2 is implemented only as a 0.95 decay on the other queues. Both a growing O(N^2) cost on long traces and a semantic drift from the published algorithm.

Policy/generator parameter mismatch: the policy assumes chat (mu, sigma) = (4.77, 1.279) (vllm/core/evictor.py:1178) while the shipped trace configs generate ShareGPT turns with (4.15, 0.971) (TaskData/Hybrid/test1/tasks_config.yaml, matching paper §6.1). Unclear from the repo whether the published numbers were produced with this mismatch.

ToolBench data is only reachable through a personal OneDrive share (TaskData/ToolBench/readme.md:1); if it rots the task must be substituted (StableToolBench on HF) or dropped, changing the trace composition.

The GPU-side result (Table 5) requires compiling the vLLM fork (VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 is the cheap route); demo/run_gpu.sh:1 hard-codes CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 (we have device 0 only) and the --enable-lmcache path in run_gpu.py:239-258 calls run_simulation twice with an unbound llm - avoid that flag.
Tokenized *_session_data.jsonl files store full token-id lists as JSON and will run to tens of GB for ShareGPT-scale inputs; ~257 GB free is comfortable but should be watched.
No artifact badge or AE appendix found for this POMACS article, so all build/run judgements above are desk predictions, not verified executions.

Concurrent work SAECache (arXiv 2605.18825, May 2026) proposes a strikingly similar multi-queue plus hit-efficiency design with online parameter adaptation; it does not cite UniCache and has no code, but it narrows the novelty of add-ons that merely make UniCache's constants adaptive.
